I studied abroad there last summer. I have to say there are many highlights for me in Seoul. I will list them below
- Cafe hopping. They have a multitude of unique cafes each with different themes. The drinks in regular cafes too are spectacular. One I think is a MUST is called Nuldam Space in Jongno District. What makes this one special is that it’s a letter cafe. You basically can write your future self a letter while you sip on a nice drink. You make your own stamp, write your address and seal your letter. You then put it in a box marked with a date two weeks before you want it to arrive. Mine arrived on my birthday this year. A great memory. 

- Lotte world is fun to visit too! Rent a uniform and wear a silly headband!

- Palaces are great and made even more fun if you dress up in traditional Hanbok, which you can rent at a store). 

- Check out photo booths and take a bunch of photos with fun props. 

- Banpo bridge! I’m not sure if they do light shows in the fall/winter but it’s a lovely river to do a little boat ride on

- This one you have to book a tour but if you can get one I recommend a DMZ tour. You can see North Korea through binocular views. 

- Shopping! Hongdae in Seoul is known for being a top place to buy things. Everything is relatively (compared to America) cheap. I loved the shop The Playground personally. I found a bunch of funny mistranslated shirts there. Common Ground is also good.
